newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst lifts 1996 EU grain crop to 201.4 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Analyst lifts 1996 EU grain crop to 201.4 mln T.

text.p: Cereals analyst Strategie Grains said on Tuesday it had raised its estimate for this year's European Union cereals harvest by 2.5 million tonnes to a record 201.4 million tonnes.

The increase, which brings the private forecaster's estimate close to recently published trade figures, comes after a new wave of upbeat crop reports from Germany, France, Britain, Denmark and Sweden, it said.
The new total represents a 14 percent increase over 1995.
In September, Strategie Grains projected grain output of 198.9 million tonnes from the EU's 15 nations this year.

In a new October report, Strategie Grains hiked its estimate for EU soft wheat harvested this summer to 90.3 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 88.1 million tonnes. The new figure is 13 percent up from last year's output of 79.9 million tonnes.
Production of barley showed the highest percentage gain of 20 percent despite a slightly lower forecast this time round.
Strategie Grains trimmed its crop estimate for barley to 52.4 million tonnes from a previous 52.5 million tonnes.
Last year's barley output was 43.7 million tonnes, it said.
Maize, which is only just starting to be harvested, is forecast at 32.9 million tonnes -- unchanged from last month's estimate and up 11 percent from last year's 29.5 million.
Strategie Grains director Andree Paquier-Defois said the new total harvest estimate of 201.4 million tonnes was a record.
Production last peaked at between 170 and 180 million tonnes in 1984, she said.

Analysts say EU output has been boosted by a host of new countries joining the trade bloc in the last decade -- Spain, Portugal, the former East Germany, Austria, Finland and Sweden -- but even including those countries in past EU statistics would barely produce a crop of 200 million tonnes.
High sowings and a surge in yields produced an unexpected boom in production this year after early problems with drought.
On October 11 the European grain trade association, Coceral, predicted an EU harvest of 201.1 million tonnes for 1996.
